Home/Postpartum Doula

Postpartum Doula Care in Long Beach & Orange County

A new baby changes the rhythm of a home. Some days you may need help with feeding or soothing; on others, a meal and a chance to shower can mean everything. I offer postpartum doula care that makes room for your needs alongside your baby’s.

Let’s Connect

Care for the parent, care for the family

As a mom of three, I know how much can fit into a single day with a newborn. My approach starts with listening: what feels hard right now, what would bring some relief, and what helps you feel like yourself? Together, we’ll find practical ways to make the early days feel more supported, without expecting your family to follow someone else’s rhythm.

What support can include

  • Hands-on newborn care, with guidance around feeding, soothing, and routines.
  • A listening ear, encouragement, and emotional support through early parenthood.
  • Help with light household tasks, meal preparation, and sibling care.
  • Education that helps you feel more confident caring for your baby.
  • Support for partners as they settle into their new roles.
  • Thoughtful resources and referrals when your family needs additional support.

Is this support right for your family?

Postpartum care is for growing families, whether you’re meeting your first baby or balancing newborn needs with older siblings. You can ask for help with everyday tasks, talk through questions, or simply have someone alongside you while you find your footing.

Serving families close to home

Based in Los Alamitos, I offer in-person postpartum doula care in Long Beach, Greater Los Angeles, and Orange County. Share your location and what support would help your family when you inquire.

Kind words from families

Your questions, answered

Can you help with things beyond baby care?

Yes. Practical support can include meal preparation, light household tasks, and sibling care. We’ll talk about your family’s needs so our time together feels helpful.

Is postpartum support only for first-time parents?

No. Welcoming another baby brings its own adjustments. Support can help you make space for your recovery, your newborn, and the rest of your family.

How do we decide what support I need?

Start by telling me a little about your family through the contact form. We can discuss your priorities, availability, and current pricing together. You don’t need a perfectly organized list before reaching out.

Let’s find your next step

You don’t have to figure it all out before we connect. Tell me what life looks like for your family and how you’d like to feel supported.
